 Search "100 Days of Deception" Episode 10: Did Ga-kyung Just Lose Everything for Love?
 Jon Lui 16 hours ago 6 min read SPOILER WARNING:  Major Episode 10 spoilers ahead, including Song Jeon's death, So-ran's injury, and Tae-woong's devastating decision. 
 Ga-kyung and Tae-woong's complicated love story takes a heartbreaking turn in Episode 10 of 100 Days of Deception . (tvN) Lee Ga-kyung ( Kim You-jung ) finally admitted her feelings for Kim Tae-woong ( Park Jin-young ), but 100 Days of Deception  isn't making it easy for these two to find happiness. In Episode 10, a failed bombing operation, a devastating loss, and an unexpected separation leave Ga-kyung facing a future that looks nothing like the one she imagined. 
 After the explosive cliffhanger in Episode 9, viewers finally learn what happens when the independence group's operation at the Government-General banquet goes horribly wrong. But while the explosion creates chaos, the emotional damage between Ga-kyung and Tae-woong may be even harder to recover from. 
 With Ga-kyung boarding a train toward her long-awaited escape to America and Tae-woong facing another brutal test under Sato Shinichi ( Jin Sun-kyu ), Episode 10 raises a painful question: Has Ga-kyung finally found something worth staying for, only to lose it? 
 1. Ga-kyung and Tae-woong's Love Story Takes a Heartbreaking Turn 
 The emotional weight of Episode 10 begins with the confession that viewers have been waiting for. 
 In Episode 9, Ga-kyung returned Tae-woong's pawn ticket and admitted, "I liked you. Kim Tae-woong." It was a rare moment of honesty from someone who has spent so much of her life hiding behind lies, disguises, and survival instincts. 
 Still from Episode 9 of 100 Days of Deception. (tvN) But Tae-woong couldn't accept her feelings. Still struggling with the truth about his adoptive father and his own identity, he insisted that he was Sato Hide-o, not Kim Tae-woong. 
 That rejection makes their brief reunion after the explosion especially painful. 
 As the banquet descends into chaos, Ga-kyung tries to move the bomb away from the crowded area. The explosion eventually sends everyone scrambling, and she catches sight of Tae-woong, who has survived the immediate blast. 
 Yet there is no happy reunion. Their eyes meet, but circumstances pull them apart again. 
 It's a cruel moment for a couple who have finally acknowledged their feelings but still cannot find a way to be together. 
 The question for fans:  Is Tae-woong pushing Ga-kyung away because he doesn't love her, or because he no longer knows how to be Kim Tae-woong? 
 2. The Bombing Operation Fails, and Song Jeon Pays the Ultimate Price 
 The independence group's carefully planned operation takes a disastrous turn. 
 Just five minutes before the bomb is scheduled to explode, Tae-woong is unexpectedly asked to interpret the governor's toast. He ends up standing dangerously close to the cake containing the explosive. 
 Stills from Episode 9 of 100 Days of Deception (tvN) Then an unexpected announcement changes everything: Japan's prime minister has been attacked in Tokyo. 
 The Japanese officials, including Sato Shinichi, immediately leave the banquet, and the event is canceled. 
 The planned assassination attempt is thrown into disarray. So-ran, visibly shaken by the failed operation, grabs a knife and leaves the banquet hall. 
 But the danger is far from over. 
 Song Jeon confronts Sato Shinichi in the aftermath, and the encounter turns violent. When Tae-woong arrives, Sato gives him a horrifying command: shoot Song Jeon. 
 The situation places Tae-woong in an impossible position. His adoptive father is demanding that he kill a member of the independence group, while the man in front of him represents everything the resistance is fighting against. 
 Gunshots ring out, and Song Jeon is killed. 
 This is one of the episode's most devastating developments. The operation has not only failed to unfold as planned but has also left the resistance group with a devastating loss. 
 3. Tae-woong's Most Cruel Test Yet: Will He Obey Sato Shinichi? 
 If there was ever a moment that exposed the impossible position Tae-woong occupies, this was it. 
 Sato Shinichi doesn't simply demand loyalty from his adoptive son. He puts him in a situation where proving that loyalty means turning against the very people who represent his Korean identity. 
 Tae-woong has already discovered the horrifying truth about his adoptive father's involvement in the massacre of Koreans. He can no longer look at Shinichi as the father he once believed he knew. 
 But escaping that relationship isn't easy. 
 Still from Episode 10 of 100 Days of Deception (tvN) When Sato orders him to shoot Song Jeon, Tae-woong faces a choice that could permanently change how the resistance group sees him — and how he sees himself. 
 His decision also adds another layer to his rejection of Ga-kyung. Perhaps he believes he has become someone she should not love. But the more he tries to embrace the identity of Sato Hide-o, the further he moves from the person Ga-kyung recognizes. 
 Can he ever break free from his adoptive father's control? 
 4. So-ran's Injury and Song Jeon's Death Could Destroy the Resistance Group 
 The consequences of the failed operation don't stop with Song Jeon. 
 When So-ran discovers his body, she is devastated. Her grief and anger are immediately visible, and the situation becomes even more dangerous when gunfire erupts. 
 Sato's men are closing in, and So-ran is shot while trying to escape with Yoo Philip ( Lee Mu-saeng ). 
 Philip manages to get her away from the immediate danger, but their situation is far from safe. 
 The two characters have been instrumental in organizing and supporting the resistance, and their involvement has always carried enormous personal risks. 
 Lee Mu-saeng as Yoo Philip in 100 Days of Deception (tvN) Now the group has lost Song Jeon, So-ran is injured, and Sato Shinichi has every reason to become more suspicious of the people around him. 
 The operation may be over, but the consequences are only beginning. 
 5. Ga-kyung Finally Boards the Train to America — But at What Cost? 
 Perhaps the most bittersweet development of Episode 10 is seeing Ga-kyung finally board the train that will take her closer to the life she has always wanted. 
 America has represented freedom and independence for Ga-kyung throughout the series. It is her chance to escape the restrictions of colonial Joseon and stop living a life dictated by other people's decisions. 
 Yet her departure doesn't feel like a victory. 
 Ga-kyung finally boards the train to America. (tvN) After the explosion, Kim Myeong-nam urges her to leave, reminding her that going to America means putting an end to everything she has been involved in. 
 Ga-kyung eventually makes her way out. 
 But viewers are left with a complicated image: a woman who has finally confessed her feelings for someone, only to leave without knowing what will happen to him. 
 Her forehead is wounded, her clothes are marked by the explosion, and her expression suggests that the journey ahead won't be as uncomplicated as she once imagined. 
 It is difficult not to wonder whether she is leaving because she still wants America or because staying has become too dangerous. 
 And what about Tae-woong? Can she really begin again without knowing whether he will ever escape Sato Shinichi? 
 6. Sato Shinichi's Next Move Could Make Everything Worse 
 The failed operation has given Sato Shinichi another reason to tighten his grip on those around him. 
 His suspicions are growing, and the raid on So-ran and Philip's home signals that the resistance group's members are no longer safe. 
 The most worrying part is that Sato has already demonstrated how far he is willing to go to maintain control over Tae-woong. 
 Still from 100 Days of Deception (tvN) With Song Jeon dead, So-ran injured, and Ga-kyung heading toward America, the resistance group is facing an uncertain future. 
 But the biggest threat may be the fact that Tae-woong is still within Sato's reach. 
 If Shinichi continues using his adoptive son as a weapon against the independence movement, Tae-woong may eventually have to decide whether he is willing to sacrifice everything to reclaim his identity. 
 Final Thoughts: Did Ga-kyung Just Lose Everything for Love? 
 Episode 10 delivers one of the drama's most emotionally complicated chapters so far. 
 The failed bombing operation and Song Jeon's death remind viewers that the fight for independence comes with devastating sacrifices. Meanwhile, Tae-woong's impossible position under Sato Shinichi makes his future increasingly uncertain. 
 But it's Ga-kyung's departure that gives the episode its emotional punch. 
 She finally said what she felt. She finally allowed herself to care about someone beyond her own survival. And just as she begins to imagine a different kind of future, she boards a train that takes her away from the person she wants to be with. 
 Still, Ga-kyung's story shouldn't be reduced to a woman choosing a man over her freedom. Her dream of America matters, too. She has every right to pursue a life beyond the dangers of Gyeongseong. 
 The real tragedy is that she and Tae-woong have yet to find a way to choose themselves — and each other — without someone else controlling their fate. 
 Now we want to know: Should Ga-kyung leave Tae-woong behind and finally pursue her dream of America, or should she fight for the man she loves? 
 Because after Episode 10, one thing is certain: their love story is far from over, but their chance at happiness has never looked more uncertain.
